france24fr.description: L'Italie a vivement réagi vendredi 19 juin aux critiques du président américain Donald Trump contre la Première ministre Giorgia Meloni rapportées dans les médias, son chef de la diplomatie annulant sa visite aux États-Unis.

france24fr.title: Sida : le Lenacapavir, un traitement préventif à l’efficacité prometteuse
france24fr.description: C’est une injection qui pourrait changer la donne. Administrée deux fois par an, elle offre une protection quasi complète (plus de 99 %) contre le virus du sida. Après des années de recherche et d’expérimentation, le Lenacapavir, soutenu par le Global Fund et le PEPFAR, a été homologué et est en passe d’être administré à grande échelle.

france24fr.title: Niger : ce que l’on sait de l’attaque jihadiste contre l’aéroport de Niamey
france24fr.description: On en sait un peu plus sur l’attaque terroriste qui a visé, jeudi 18 juin 2026, une base militaire située au sein de l’aéroport international Diori Hamani de Niamey. Au soir des faits, l’armée nigérienne a communiqué un bilan officiel après plusieurs heures d’opérations de ratissage. Revendiquée par le Groupe de soutien à l’islam et aux musulmans (JNIM), affilié à Al-Qaïda, l’attaque a été repoussée par les Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS) après plus de deux heures de violents affrontement

france24fr.title: Un manuscrit inédit de Mozart, petit trésor mis en musique à Paris
france24fr.description: C'est une rare découverte : un cahier de composition de Mozart, sept pièces pour flûte et harpe et des leçons qu'il donnait à la duchesse de Guînes, a été retrouvé grâce à la persévérance d'un conservateur de la Bibliothèque nationale de France (BnF).

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : les États-Unis en 16es, le Brésil et le Maroc s'en rapprochent
france24fr.description: Au lendemain de la qualification du Mexique, les États-Unis, autres coorganisateurs du Mondial 2026, ont à leur tour validé vendredi leur billet pour les 16es de finale, dont se rapprochent aussi le Brésil et le Maroc.

france24fr.title: Chaleur : la canicule s'étend, vigilance rouge en vue dimanche
france24fr.description: Oraux du bac perturbés, prudence de mise sur les chantiers et lors de la Fête de la musique : la canicule a continué à s'étendre vendredi 19 juin, avec 53 départements placés en vigilance orange, bientôt 60 samedi, et un niveau "rouge" qui pourrait être déclenché dimanche dans certaines zones.

france24fr.title: Pologne : le président annonce retirer la plus haute distinction du pays à Zelensky
france24fr.description: Le président polonais, Karol Nawrocki, a annoncé vendredi 19 juin qu'il retirait la plus haute distinction du pays au président ukrainien, Volodymyr Zelensky, l'Ordre de l'Aigle blanc, sur fond de tensions liées à l'histoire commune des deux États voisins.

france24fr.title: Frappes au Liban : "Il y a une violation de l'accord signé par Trump et Pezeshkian"
france24fr.description: La rencontre en Suisse avec J.D. Vance pour discuter de l'application de l'accord signé par Trump et Pezeshkian pour mettre fin à la guerre au Moyen-Orient, prévue ce vendredi 19 juin, a été annulée. "Tant que la guerre n'est pas arrêtée au Liban, il n'est pas question de discuter avec les Américains" du côté iranien, rapporte notre correspondant Siavosh Ghazi.

france24fr.title: Europe : comment les crises énergétiques accélèrent les renouvelables
france24fr.description:
🚛💨 En Belgique, des camions sont désormais rechargés grâce à l'énergie du vent stockée dans des batteries.
 
Face aux crises énergétiques et aux tensions géopolitiques, les énergies renouvelables ne sont plus seulement un enjeu climatique : elles deviennent aussi un enjeu de souveraineté énergétique.

france24fr.title: Avec sa Cité internationale, Annecy devient capitale mondiale de l’animation "toute l’année"
france24fr.description: Pendant tout le week-end, Annecy fête l’ouverture de sa toute nouvelle Cité internationale du cinéma d'animation, un projet à 54,5 millions d’euros qui regroupe notamment un musée, des ateliers d'initiation à l'image par image, un cinéma et une résidence d'artistes. Entretien avec la directrice Culture Peggy Zejgman-Lecarme.

france24fr.title: Vingt ans du Quai Branly : retour sur l'histoire du musée qui fait "dialoguer les cultures"
france24fr.description: Inauguré le 20 juin 2006, le musée du Quai Branly, dédié aux arts premiers et aux cultures du monde entier, célèbre son vingtième anniversaire en grande pompe de vendredi à dimanche. Expositions marquantes, polémiques, restitution des biens culturels pillés pendant la colonisation, France 24 revient sur les grands moments de l'histoire de l'établissement parisien voulu par Jacques Chirac.

france24fr.title: "J'étais nul à l'école"... Et si l'école passait aussi par les mains ?
france24fr.description: Décrochage, échec scolaire, métiers manuels : et si certains élèves apprenaient mieux avec leurs mains qu'avec les méthodes traditionnelles de l'école ?

À suivre sur YouTube lors de cette troisième journée de salon, samedi : un atelier "tournage et montage sur le terrain", une master class sur les promesses de l'investigation open source (Osint), et une autre sur l'IA et la désinformation.

france24fr.title: Bolivie : le président Paz décrète l'état d'exception après plus de six semaines de contestation
france24fr.description: Le président bolivien Rodrigo Paz a décrété l'état d'exception, samedi, après plus de six semaines de contestation sociale, qui s'est traduite par des affrontements entre policiers et manifestants et des blocages routiers. L'état d'exception autorise notamment le gouvernement à recourir aux forces armées sur tout le territoire national. Cette décision intervient alors que Rodrigo Paz vient de conclure un accord avec la COB, la principale organisation syndicale du pays.

zeit.description: Nichts ist sicher. Außer der Tod, Steuern und dass schottische Fans bei einer WM die Biervorräte leeren. Unser Kolumnist kämpft mit Bewunderung und Neid.

zeit.description: In München ist ein Güterzug von einer Brücke fünf Meter in die Tiefe gestürzt. Die Polizei sprach von einem Toten. Einschränkungen im Fernverkehr gibt es nicht.

nzz.title: «Wir schicken den iranischen Ayatollahs 300 Milliarden Dollar?» – Trumps Iran-Abkommen spaltet die Republikaner

nzz.title: Gutes Timing oder Glück? Der Benzinpreis fällt rechtzeitig zur amerikanischen Feriensaison
nzz.description: Donald Trump kann vorerst aufatmen: Der Spritpreis an Amerikas Tankstellen ist unter die psychologische Marke von 4 Dollar pro Gallone gefallen. Ob der Frieden mit Iran seinen Republikanern die Zwischenwahlen im Herbst rettet, bleibt ungewiss.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - 36 Grad, und es wird noch heisser: Die Hitze hat weite Teile Europas fest im Griff
nzz.description: In der Schweiz und weiten Teilen Europas werden sehr hohe Temperaturen gemessen. Länder wie Spanien, Frankreich und die Schweiz haben für das Wochenende Hitzewarnungen herausgegeben.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Die EU würde China gerne den Meister zeigen, aber für eine echte Konfrontation fehlt ihr der Hebel
nzz.description: Am EU-Gipfel von dieser Woche waren Chinas unfaire Handelspraktiken das grosse Thema. Die 27 Regierungschefs wollen sich wehren. Sie haben aber bloss die Wahl zwischen Pest und Cholera.

nzz.description: Die USA erhöhen den Druck auf die anderen Industrieländer und fordern eine höhere Beteiligung an den Kosten für Arzneimittel.

observador.title: O melhor Mundial da Seleção entre as lágrimas de Eusébio
observador.description: Os heróis não foram só os jogadores – Pickles encontrou o troféu do Mundial nuns arbustos. Para a história fica o recorde de Eusébio, que ainda hoje perdura, e a única vez que a Inglaterra foi feliz.

observador.title: Histórico: Almirón é o primeiro expulso pela lei Prestianni
observador.description: Depois de ter estado na primeira reversão de um cartão amarelo por simulação, Miguel Almirón foi o primeiro expulso à luz da nova regra "Prestianni" que proíbe que jogadores tapem a boca para falar.

observador.title: Montenegro discursa no arranque do congresso do PSD
observador.description: Depois do chumbo da reforma laboral, PSD a Anadia para dois dias de congresso. Montenegro faz o discurso de abertura.

observador.title: O português que gere um dos hotéis ingleses mais luxuosos
observador.description: Tem mais de 500 funcionários, há 25 anos que não passa o Natal com a família e no Grantley Hall até controla o estacionamento ao milímetro. Quem é ele, como chegou até aqui e o que lhe falta alcançar?

observador.title: Presidente da Bolívia decreta "estado de emergência"
observador.description: O anúncio da medida ocorreu horas depois de o executivo chegar a um acordo com a Central Operária Boliviana (COB) para pôr fim às mobilizações que se iniciaram há 50 dias.

observador.title: Mais de duas mil queixas sobre táxis e TVDE
observador.description: Os principais motivos de reclamação apresentados este ano pelos consumidores foram a faturação, o cumprimento defeituoso, o atendimento e os pagamentos.

observador.description: Protesto acontece esta tarde, em Lisboa. Ainda neste jornal, mulher morre e 1.700 pessoas são retiradas de um resort na República Dominicana após um incêndio.

observador.title: República Dominicana. Incêndio em resort mata uma mulher
observador.description: Hóspedes do hotel em que deflagrou incêndio de grandes dimensões foram realojados em unidades próximas. Uma mulher morreu e três pessoas tiveram de ser hospitalizadas.

observador.title: “Party in the USA!”. Brasil já samba. Ronaldo “focus”
observador.description: Enquanto Portugal prepara o duelo com o Uzbequistão, Ronaldo volta à deixar mensagem nas redes sociais e Rúben Dias afasta "ruído". Os EUA vencem e já estão apurados. O Brasil ganha ao Haiti.

observador.title: GNR reforça patrulhamento para prevenir incêndios
observador.description: Será ainda assegurada videovigilância remota, através da monitorização contínua de cerca de sete milhões de hectares através de uma rede fixa composta por 147 torres.

observador.title: Dia 10 do Mundial-2026 começa com jogo grande entre europeus
observador.description: Portugal regressa aos trabalhos em Palm Beach, tendo em vista o jogo com o Uzbequistão. Dia 10 terá quatro jogos que começam com o Países Baixos-Suécia e têm logo a seguir a Alemanha. Siga em direto.

observador.title: Mesmo com cessar-fogo, ataques das IDF relatados no Líbano
observador.description: Pelo menos cinco pessoas morreram esta manhã num ataque aéreo israelita na cidade de Arabsalim, no sul do Líbano, apesar do cessar-fogo acordado ontem entre Israel e o Hezbollah.

observador.title: 9h. Termómetros chegam hoje perto dos 40 graus
observador.description: Há oito distritos do interior norte, centro e Alentejo sob aviso amarelo do IPMA. Ainda, Está marcada para hoje, em Lisboa, uma manifestação contra o desfecho do caso Odair Moniz.

observador.title: Guerra e reformas; Rui Ramos e José Manuel Fernandes
observador.description: O acordo de paz, a incapacidade de Portugal fazer reformas, e as perguntas a José Manuel Fernandes e Rui Ramos sobre o assunto.

observador.description: “Sem justiça não há paz” é o lema da manifestação em Lisboa, que este sábado fará o percurso entre o Largo de São Domingos, de onde sairá às 17h00, e o Largo José Saramago.

observador.title: 8h. Novos ataques de Israel no sul do Líbano
observador.description: Apesar do cessar-fogo em vigor, as operações das Forças de Defesa Israelitas continuam a atacar o Líbano. Ainda, o enviado especial de Donald Trump para o Médio Oriente vai viajar hoje para a Suíça.

observador.title: Inês, a viajante solitária
observador.description: Inês Amaral gosta de viajar sozinha e escreveu um livro a pensar nos viajantes solitários. Vive no Reino Unido, país a partir do qual tem partido para inúmeras viagens pelo mundo.

spiegel.title: Taylor Swift und Travis Kelce: Wird da etwa doch schon geheiratet?
spiegel.description: Die Promihochzeit des Jahres steht an und die Gerüchteküche brodelt. Wann und wo geben sich Taylor Swift und Travis Kelce da Jawort? Neueste Fotos zeigen nun offenbar Hochzeitsvorbereitungen nahe Swifts Anwesen in Rhode Island.

spiegel.title: München: Ein Mensch stirbt bei Güterzug-Unfall in Milbertshofen
spiegel.description: In der Nacht sind in München zwei Güterzüge auf einer Brücke kollidiert. Dabei stürzten zwei Waggons fünf Meter in die Tiefe. Ein Mensch ist bei dem Unfall ums Leben gekommen.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Miguel Almirón aus Paraguay sieht gegen die Türkei die Rote Karte
spiegel.description: Rudelbildung, Spieler diskutieren und halten sich die Hand vor den Mund – eine typische Szene im modernen Fußball. Doch das ist mittlerweile verboten, wie Paraguays Miguel Almirón bei der WM erfahren musste.

spiegel.title: Reformen: Wirtschaftsweise Monika Schnitzer fordert Sparmaßnahmen
spiegel.description: Pflege, Mehrwertsteuer, Diesel: Im Reformstreit wächst der Druck auf die Bundesregierung. Hier macht Wirtschaftsweisen-Chefin Monika Schnitzer konkrete Sparvorschläge – und sagt, was für die Menschen teurer werden könnte.

spiegel.title: Rastatt: Blitzeinschlag während Handballfest – neun Verletzte
spiegel.description: Sie zelteten auf einem Sportplatz, als der Blitz einschlug: Bei einem Handballfest in Rastatt sind neun Menschen verletzt worden, sechs von ihnen wurden ins Krankenhaus gebracht.

spiegel.title: Kinmen: Hier ist Taiwan so, wie China es sich wünscht
spiegel.description: Die taiwanische Insel Kinmen ist nur drei Kilometer von der chinesischen Küste entfernt. Der Konflikt mit Peking wirkt hier wie Folklore.

spiegel.title: Hochwasser in Rheinland-Pfalz: Rhein-Lahn-Kreis von Fluten betroffen
spiegel.description: Unwetter und Starkregen haben in Rheinland-Pfalz zu schweren Überschwemmungen geführt. Besonders betroffen ist der Rhein-Lahn-Kreis.

spiegel.title: Österreich: Ex-Außenministerin Karin Kneissl wirft FPÖ Mobbing vor
spiegel.description: Die rechtsradikale FPÖ machte sie einst zur Ministerin, auf ihrer Hochzeit tanzte sie mit Machthaber Putin. Nun verbreitet Karin Kneissl Kremlpropaganda – und schimpft neuerdings über die FPÖ.

spiegel.title: Sebastian Klussmann: Wie wir uns mehr Wissen aneignen - Podcast
spiegel.description: Stumpfes Auswendiglernen bringt wenig. Quiz-Europameister Sebastian Klussmann erklärt, wie sich unsere Allgemeinbildung selbst an der Wursttheke erweitern lässt.

spiegel.title: Libanon meldet mindestens fünf Tote bei israelischen Angriffen
spiegel.description: Erst am Freitag hatten die USA verkündet, dass sich Israel und die libanesische Hisbollah-Miliz auf eine Waffenruhe verständigt haben. Nun hat Israel laut Beirut erneut Angriffe auf den Südlibanon geflogen.

spiegel.title: Umgang mit Israel: Linke macht Völkermord-Vorwurf gegen Israel zur Parteilinie
spiegel.description: Die Haltung zum Nahostkonflikt ist in der Linken seit jeher umstritten. Auf ihrem Parteitag in Potsdam haben die Delegierten die Position deutlich verschärft.

spiegel.title: Gute Nachrichten: Kochen ohne »koloniale Zutaten«, Steuererklärung, WM-Fans aus Schottland
spiegel.description: In diesem Restaurant in Minneapolis gibt es Gerichte mit einer Kampfansage. Keine Lust auf Steuererklärung? Mit diesen Tipps läuft’s. Und: Schottische WM-Fans begeistern Boston (und die Welt). Die guten Nachrichten der Woche.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Deutschland vs. Elfenbeinküste - Das deutsche Standard-Geheimnis
spiegel.description: Bei dieser WM sind Freistöße und Ecken ein Schlüssel zum DFB-Erfolg und können auch gegen die Elfenbeinküste entscheidend sein. Spezialtrainer Mads Buttgereit arbeitet mit Apps und Daten. Ein Blick hinter die Kulissen.

spiegel.title: Daaden: Kinder retten Zweijährigen im Freibad
spiegel.description: Eine Gruppe Kinder hat im rheinland-pfälzischen Daaden einem Kleinkind das Leben gerettet. Die Sieben- und Achtjährigen sahen das Kind regungslos im Wasser treiben und griffen sofort ein.

spiegel.title: E-Mobilität: Was Kfz-Meister zur richtigen Wartung von E-Autos raten
spiegel.description: Wer elektrisch fährt, kann an Reparaturen sparen – doch manchen machen Unwissen und Unsicherheit einen Strich durch die Rechnung. Das raten auf E-Autos spezialisierte Kfz-Meister.

spiegel.title: Lyten will Northvolt-Überreste bei Heide für 60 Millionen Euro übernehmen
spiegel.description: Mit reichlich Staatsförderung wollte die schwedische Firma Northvolt eine riesige Batteriezellfabrik in Schleswig-Holstein bauen. Nach der Pleite übernimmt nun das Start-up Lyten die Überreste – für einen Bruchteil des investierten Geldes.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump und sein Reflecting Pool: Von Königsblau zu Algengrün
spiegel.description: Donald Trump wollte in Washington den allegorischen Sumpf austrocknen. Inzwischen hat er mit Steuermitteln einen ganz realen geschaffen: Der Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool hat sich algengrün verfärbt.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Deutschland gegen die Elfenbeinküste - wen würden Sie aufstellen?
spiegel.description: Das 7:1 gegen Curaçao war ein perfekter WM-Start für die DFB-Elf. Da muss man doch im zweiten Vorrundenduell gegen die Elfenbeinküste nichts ändern, oder? Andererseits ist da ja noch der Fall Deniz Undav.

They identified 18 distinct cell type clusters in the inflorescence meristem (the stem cell niche at the tip of the flowering shoot) that generates a plant's above-ground organs, such as stems and flowers.

phys-org.title: How H5N1 bird flu hid unrecognized for weeks in dairy cattle
phys-org.description: When H5N1 bird flu first began infecting U.S. cattle in early 2024, diagnosis was elusive because, in cows, the disease looked completely different. Instead of affecting the lungs, as H5N1 does in other mammalian species, it caused severe infection in the cows' udders, largely sparing the lungs.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

proj-syn.title: How (Not) to Conserve Tropical Forests
proj-syn.description: Although the Tropical Forest Forever Facility that emerged from the last United Nations Climate Conference is unlikely to succeed, critically important global conservation efforts are not doomed. Through sustainability-linked sovereign bonds and loans, tropical countries can overcome the TFFF’s fatal flaws.

proj-syn.title: Was Brexit Inevitable?
proj-syn.description: If counterfactual history is motivated by a refusal to accept what many have deemed inevitable, it is newly relevant now that the West is marking the tenth anniversary of the Brexit referendum. Even if Britain's fateful choice was caused by deeper structural and historical forces, that does not justify fatalism.

proj-syn.title: Questioning the Just War Doctrine
proj-syn.description: With war becoming more frequent and more lethal to civilians, Pope Leo XIV and the College of Cardinals are wading into the debate over its legitimacy. The best outcome of the “consistory” Leo is convening in in late June would be to authorize an overhaul of the just war doctrine for the modern era—and ask the necessary questions.

proj-syn.title: Bosnia Must Stand on Its Own
proj-syn.description: The Trump administration's recent, apparently corrupt intervention in Bosnia and Herzegovina could have been an opportunity finally to put the country on a path to full independence after more than 30 years of being a ward of the international community. Instead, the vicious cycle of dependence looks set to continue.

proj-syn.title: The Strategic Logic of the AI Arms Race
proj-syn.description: AI and drones are rapidly transforming warfare, shifting military power toward countries that can combine manufacturing scale, advanced AI systems, and battlefield data. The United States and Europe, hobbled by political dysfunction and obsolete military structures, remain dangerously unprepared.

proj-syn.title: The Meaning of Limited Government—Then and Now
proj-syn.description: In 1776, Adam Smith and America’s founders envisioned an economy that allowed individuals to pursue their own material well-being, with minimal government intervention. Today, America’s Republican Party claims to be committed to restoring that laissez-faire ideal, even as they make a mockery of its animating principles.

proj-syn.title: AI Sovereignty Is About Options, Not Ownership
proj-syn.description: The US government’s abrupt decision to suspend foreign access to Anthropic’s Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models clarifies what “AI sovereignty” is really about. In the emerging AI economy, competitive advantage will come not from owning a single model, but from being able to evaluate, select, and orchestrate many models.

proj-syn.title: The Promise and Peril of AGI
proj-syn.description: Artificial general intelligence could dramatically increase human prosperity and free people from countless mundane tasks. But unless its benefits and ownership are broadly shared, it could deprive billions of workers of their livelihoods and pave the way for a new form of techno-authoritarianism.

proj-syn.title: Reversing Brexit Is Labour’s Best Hope
proj-syn.description: When it comes to the relationship between the United Kingdom and the European Union, political expediency and economic logic both point in the same direction. A majority of British voters now believe that Brexit was a mistake, and they are looking for a leader who will put the issue back on the national agenda.

proj-syn.title: Global Health Reform Must Bolster Innovation
proj-syn.description: As funding falls for global public health, calls for a country-led system have grown louder. Such reforms are necessary, but they must not come at the expense of new vaccines, medicines, and diagnostics, which can be delivered by strengthening mechanisms—such as product development partnerships—that already work.

proj-syn.title: Learning from the Right Sovereign Wealth Funds
proj-syn.description: The Gulf has made establishing a sovereign wealth fund seem like a strategic—and glamorous—choice, leading countries like Canada to launch their own. But Latin America has run this experiment many times over the years, offering a more realistic view of an SWF’s pitfalls and promise.

proj-syn.title: Europe Cannot Afford Another Lost Year
proj-syn.description: European businesses need simpler rules, faster permitting, affordable energy, stronger infrastructure, and a fully functioning single market. The longer that European policymakers fail to deliver on these policies, the greater Europe’s competitiveness challenge will become.

proj-syn.title: White House Fight Night
proj-syn.description: The venue on the South Lawn for UFC Freedom 250 was built, approved, lit, filmed, defended, watched, and enjoyed as part of a celebration of freedom. President Donald Trump’s chosen object to represent that celebration was a cage.

proj-syn.title: The US-Iran Agreement Is a First Step
proj-syn.description: While the recently announced US-Iranian memorandum of understanding is certainly good news, it is not definitive. The path from a statement of diplomatic intent to a fully restored, non-inflationary energy supply chain is fraught with political, technical, and physical risks.

proj-syn.title: Developing-Country Risk Is Being Mispriced
proj-syn.description: When investors say there are no “bankable” projects in developing economies, they are typically referring less to project quality than to the cost of capital. But the assumptions driving up risk premia are not supported by the evidence, and until this changes, the misallocation of capital will continue to undermine development.

proj-syn.title: The Fed Has Been Honest and Stupid
proj-syn.description: It would be easy—and a mistake—to blame the US Federal Reserve’s many blunders on corrupt bureaucrats or imagined conspiracies. The truth of the matter is that the central bank relies on an outdated regional map and lagging indicators that no longer tell the whole story, while battling macroeconomic blazes that politicians stoke.

proj-syn.title: A New Framework for Climate Displacement
proj-syn.description: Global warming is already uprooting communities and impoverishing people who remain in vulnerable areas—a crisis that is often overshadowed by the focus on decarbonization. But the Global Climate Mobility Principles offer policymakers a framework for ensuring that these individuals maintain their agency and rights.

proj-syn.title: Peace With Iran Is All About Lebanon Now
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump says that he "calls the shots" on negotiating with Iran, and Israel has no choice but to submit to a deal that undermines its security interests. But a deal that makes Trump the protector of Lebanon—and, by extension, Iran-backed Hezbollah—could put the US and Israel on a collision course.

crunchbase.title: The Boardroom Blind Spot: When Success Hides Disruption
crunchbase.description: Boards should not wait for poor performance before confronting disruptive technologies like AI and quantum computing. Instead, writes guest columnist and strategic adviser Itay Sagie, they should evaluate the cost of inaction, challenge successful business models while they are still thriving, and proactively imagine how a technology-driven competitor could disrupt their company.

crunchbase.title: ‘This System Wasn’t Built For Me’: Black Founders Became Investors To Change Venture Capital
crunchbase.description: The consistently low numbers of U.S. venture funding to Black founders led some to turn to investing in an effort to help level the playing field. Crunchbase News talked with two such founders to hear more about their experiences in raising capital and what they’ve learned from investing.

crunchbase.title: I Sold My AI Startup Before Revenue: Here’s What Investors Missed — And Founders Shouldn’t
crunchbase.description: The greatest long-term value in AI will come from companies solving deep technical challenges at the model and infrastructure level rather than application-layer products built on existing AI platforms, writes angel investor Alexander Kardos-Nyheim. In this guest commentary he shares processes and questions he uses to determine the investability of an AI startup.

crunchbase.title: SpaceX Acquires AI Coding Tool Cursor For $60B In Year’s Largest Startup M&A Deal
crunchbase.description: The acquisition of Cursor gives SpaceX a foothold into the enterprise software development market, where AI-assisted coding has taken off and led large companies to significantly pare back their reliance on human engineers.

crunchbase.title: Silicon Is Back: Playground Global’s Decade-Long Bet On Hardware, Energy And Deep Tech Looks Prescient
crunchbase.description: In the decade-plus since Playground Global's founding, it has built its investment thesis around the idea that breakthroughs in science and engineering — not just software — would create the next generation of valuable companies. Company co-founder Peter Barrett breaks it down in this Crunchbase News Q&A.

crunchbase.title: Rewriting Your Pitch: SaaS Isn’t Dead, But The Playbook For Founders Is Changing
crunchbase.description: Because AI and LLMs are reshaping the traditional SaaS model, founders are forced to focus less on software alone and more on delivering measurable business outcomes, defensible workflow ownership, strong retention, and efficient growth. Crunchbase guest author, Ivan Nikkhoo argues that rather than chasing trends like adding services, founders should build deep moats, understand customer workflows, adapt pricing toward usage- or outcome-based models, and prove that AI creates lasting value.

crunchbase.title: The AI Startup Funding Boom Is Not A Global Phenomenon
crunchbase.description: So far in 2026, U.S. companies have pulled in nearly 80% of global seed- through growth-stage financing, per Crunchbase data. That’s a sharp divergence from the years leading up to the AI boom, when American companies typically secured less than half of all investment.
